newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN IPO - Medicorp Technologies India Ltd.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN IPO - Medicorp Technologies India Ltd.

text.p: Research supplied by Sebastian Dominic of Resource Base, a New Delhi-based private investment consultancy firm. Tel: 578 0840. This data is for investor information only and does not constitute a recommendation by Reuters.

Medicorp Technologies is coming out with this public issue to finance a project to manufacture bulk drugs, to meet the working capital requirements and to meet the expenses of the issue. Promoters of the company - the Shriram Group is engaged in hire purchase, lease financing and chit funds.

The project includes establishing a pilot plant facility and a multipurpose bulk drug and drug intermediates manufacturing facility. The pilot plant established through acquisition of plant and machinery of an existing unit is operational and will initially manufacture alprazolam and cisapride. The bulk drug unit conforming to international standards will have the built-in flexibility for change in product mix.

According to the project appraisel by ICICI, in 1995 the total estimated cost was 216 million rupees. The company could not adhere to the implementation schedule on account of the need to incorporate U.S. FDA requirements into the plant design and inclusion of four new products. Consequently there was a time overrun of eight months and the increase in project cost of 82 million rupees.

The revised project cost of 298 million rupees will be financed through 121 million rupees equity share capital and 177 million rupees loans. Out of the equity component promoters bring in 55 million rupees, ICICI 7.50 million rupees, SCICI 2.50 million rupees and 56 million rupees is to be collected from the public. Loans consists of 75 million rupees from ICICI, 35 million rupees from SCICI, 32 million rupees from IRBI and 35 million rupees unsecured loans from promoters.

The unit will have the flexibility to manufacture a whole range of products with individual capacity varying from one to five tonnes per month. The criterion for manufacturing any drug for the company will be that the product should have a substantial domestic market with a value addition potential of over 500 rupees per kg, a good export market and an off-patent status or soon to become an off-patent status. Some of the products proposed to be manufactured are terfenadine, asternizole, fluoxetine, cetirizine, ofloxacin, ciprofloxacin and enrofloxacin.

The company propose to export a major portion of its production and is negotiating with foreign companies for international marketing. In the domestic market the company will be marketing the bulk drugs directly to the users.
